$comment: EBU R 128 as a constraint set for the PROGRAMME content class. Short-form content (adverts, promos, trailers, interstitials) is governed by R 128 s1 instead — see ebu-r128-s1.json — because R 128 recommends (q) delegates it there and s1 states a different envelope. Every constraint below is quoted from R 128-2023 (v5).
name: EBU R 128

document.title: EBU R 128 — Loudness normalisation and permitted maximum level of audio signals

assets.audio.loudness.standards[].target.quote: that the Programme Loudness Level shall be normalised to a Target Level of −23.0 LUFS. Where attaining the Target Level is not achievable practically (for example, live programmes), a tolerance of ±1.0 LU is permitted. A broadcaster should ensure that a deviation from the Target Level towards the limits of the tolerance does not become standard practice;
assets.audio.loudness.standards[].target.note: −23.0 LUFS is the constant the recommendation is built on: a spec that sets a different target is not doing R 128. Recommends (j) does permit normalising LOWER than −23.0 on purpose, but requires that 'this exception shall be clearly indicated' — in UMDP terms that is a named variant of R 128, not R 128, so the editor locks the field rather than offering the exception as a value.

assets.audio.loudness.standards[].tolera.quote: Where attaining the Target Level is not achievable practically (for example, live programmes), a tolerance of ±1.0 LU is permitted. [...] that for the implementation of Loudness workflows (for example, in Quality Control environments) a tolerance of ±0.2 LU is allowed in order to take account of measurement errors;
assets.audio.loudness.standards[].tolera.note: ±1.0 LU is the loosest R 128 permits, and only for programmes where the target is not practically achievable; ±0.2 LU is the allowance for QC measurement error. A stricter house tolerance is inside the standard. A looser one is not R 128.

assets.audio.loudness.true_peak_max.quote: and that the True Peak Level of a programme shall not exceed −1 dBTP (dB True Peak) during production (linear audio), measured with a meter compliant with ITU-R BS.1770 and EBU Tech 3341. The measurement tolerance is ±0.3 dB (for signals with a bandwidth limited to 20 kHz). Permitted Maximum True Peak Levels may be lower for different distribution systems and data reduction rates.
assets.audio.loudness.true_peak_max.note: The recommendation itself sanctions a lower ceiling for a given distribution path (and refers the reader to EBU Tech 3344 for the figures), so a spec below −1 dBTP is R 128-conformant. Above it is not.

assets.audio.loudness.standards[].lra_ma.quote: that the measure Loudness Range (measured in compliance with EBU Tech 3342) may be used to evaluate the loudness variation of a programme, its potential subsequent dynamic treatment and the dynamic integrity of a distribution path;
assets.audio.loudness.standards[].lra_ma.note: R 128 recommends measuring Loudness Range but sets no ceiling, so any value here is the spec's own requirement, not the standard's. Footnote 2 discourages the measure for programmes shorter than one minute.
